title: Imperial Marriage Ceremony
next_chapter_hook: The Chief Imperial Physician trembled as he wrote the diagnosis — life force severed, beyond salvation. Yet just as everyone mourned, the fingertips of that "corpse" seemed to twitch slightly.

text.content: Three knocks, unhurried and measured, like following some rhythm. The teacup in Chen Ji's hand hovered mid-air, a cold light flickering in his eyes. At this hour, in this secluded Servants' Quarters, no one should be visiting. He slowly set down the teacup, fingers unconsciously caressing the fragment in his sleeve — the Tianji Record was faintly burning, as if warning him of something. Who was outside the door? Had the plan gone awry, or had someone moved earlier than anticipated?

dialogue.content: "It's me." A cold female voice came from outside. "Open the door." Chen Ji's eyes flickered. This voice was all too familiar to him — Su Qingyao, Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, the one most likely to see through his disguise. He rose and opened the door to find Su Qingyao in a plain white dress standing under the moonlight, her expression even colder than usual. Her gaze swept across his meager dwelling before settling on his face: "Tomorrow's ceremony, are you really going?"

"I have no choice." Chen Ji stepped aside, his voice calm. "The Crown Prince personally presides, the Xuanwu Sect Young Master comes to observe — if I don't attend, isn't that showing disrespect to the imperial court?" He paused, the corner of his mouth lifting slightly. "Besides, didn't Senior Sister Su receive an invitation too?" Su Qingyao's brow furrowed, as if about to speak, but instead simply pressed a jade slip into his hand: "Act according to circumstances tomorrow." With that, she vanished like a specter into the night.

text.content: The following day, the Imperial Marriage Ceremony. The Tianqing Sect Martial Arena was adorned with lanterns and banners, red silk carpeted the ground, celestial cranes circled above the dome, and spiritual energy flowed like threads. Chen Ji stood at the end of the servants' line, dressed in gray cloth garments, utterly unremarkable. His gaze swept across the crowd to the elevated platform — the Crown Prince in bright yellow imperial robes, face jade-like, chatting cheerfully with Xuanwu Sect Young Master Han Lie. Beside the Crown Prince stood an elderly man in court official robes, hands clasped behind his back, his sharp gaze scrutinizing everyone present.

dialogue.content: Han Lie suddenly stopped laughing, his gaze sweeping the crowd like lightning. His eyes lingered on Chen Ji for a moment before a contemptuous smile curved his lips: "That废物 came too?" His voice wasn't loud, but it carried just enough for those nearby to hear. "The Tianqing Sect has truly declined, even servants can attend the ceremony." The surrounding disciples dared not speak out in anger, some even secretly glancing at Chen Ji with pity in their eyes. Chen Ji acted as if he hadn't heard, merely lowering his eyes slightly, fingers quietly pressing against the fragment in his sleeve.

choice.prompt: Han Lie publicly humiliated him — how should one respond?

choices.description: Revealing strength at this moment is too early; better wait for the right moment. The true humiliation must come at the most critical moment.
choices.visible_reward: Hide one's strength and wait for the best opportunity

text.content: Chen Ji slowly raised his head, his gaze calm as a deep pool — no anger, no resentment, only a chilling indifference that made hearts race. He spoke softly: "Young Master Han speaks truly." Four words, neither servile nor arrogant. Han Lie frowned, as if his punch had hit cotton, and coldly snorted before turning away. The surrounding disciples looked at each other in bewilderment; some secretly shook their heads — this废物 probably won't amount to anything in this lifetime.

choices.description: A废物persona still needs废物dignity, using silk-wrapped-needle rhetoric to put him in an untenable position.
choices.visible_reward: Test the waters and make Han Lie suffer
choices.risk_hint: May reveal that you are not truly a废物

text.content: Chen Ji raised his head, a faint smile playing at the corners of his mouth: "Young Master Han is right, a废物should indeed have废物self-awareness. However —" his voice paused slightly, "I heard that Xuanwu Sect lost three elders in the Demon Abyss last month; I wonder if that counts as'废物'doings?" At these words, Han Lie's expression changed dramatically. Silence fell over the surroundings, someone inhaled sharply. This news had been tightly sealed — how would a servant disciple know about it?

Just as the atmosphere grew tense, the ceremony announcer on the high platform cried out loudly: "The auspicious hour has arrived — Please, His Highness the Crown Prince, read the Imperial Marriage Decree!" Crown Prince Li Xuanming stepped forward, unfurling a bright yellow imperial edict. His gaze swept across the crowd, lingering on Chen Ji for an instant, a complex light flickering in his eyes: "By the mandate of heaven, the emperor decrees: Tianqing Sect disciple Chen Ji, of virtuous character and gentle nature, is hereby granted an imperial marriage to—"

dialogue.content: Just then, Tianqing Sect's old sect master Ling Yuan suddenly interrupted: "Wait!" He stepped forward with his cane, his murky old eyes suddenly gleaming with sharp light. "Your Highness, this old man has a question — what merit does this Chen Ji, merely a servant, possess to receive such imperial grace? This old man has led Tianqing for a hundred years and never seen anything so absurd!" At these words, the entire venue erupted in uproar. The Crown Prince frowned slightly: "Sect Master Ling, this is my father's will." Ling Yuan pressed on unyieldingly: "Your Highness, forgive me — this old man does not doubt imperial grace, but this marriage came so mysteriously that I must inquire!"

text.content: Chen Ji watched Ling Yuan's solemn appearance, a cold smile forming in his heart. This old sect master ostensibly questioned the marriage, but in truth merely wanted to seize this opportunity to publicly humiliate him and pressure the Crown Prince. After all, beneath his "废物" disguise, no one would believe he deserved an imperial marriage. Unfortunately, none of them knew that everything had long been within his calculations. He gently closed his eyes; the Tianji Record Fragment in his sleeve quietly trembled — the Foresight Ability activated, and images from the next three hours flowed into his mind like water.

dialogue.content: In the foresight vision, the ceremony proceeded as planned, but the moment the Crown Prince finished reading the decree, he suddenly felt his气血 churning — that was the fake death pill taking effect. He had to create the illusion of "going berserk" before that, making everything appear natural. Chen Ji opened his eyes, gazing toward a certain direction in the crowd, and nodded lightly. Su Qingyao received the signal; worry flickered in her beautiful eyes, but she still微微颔首, signaling that everything was ready.

text.content: The Crown Prince continued reading the decree: "—is hereby granted an imperial marriage to Han Xuening, sister of Xuanwu Sect's Han Lie, to be married on a selected date!" At these words, Han Lie's expression changed dramatically. He猛地turned to look at Ling Yuan, the latter's eyes flashing with satisfaction — as expected, this marriage was indeed a conspiracy against Xuanwu Sect! However, before he could make a move, a commotion suddenly arose in the crowd.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji suddenly clutched his chest, his face draining of color. His body convulsed violently, a thread of blood seeping from the corner of his mouth, dripping down his chin to the ground. 'Ptoo—' He spat out a large mouthful of blood, his entire body collapsing backward, twitching incessantly on the ground. 'He's fallen into demonic possession!' someone exclaimed. 'His meridians are reversing!' Amidst the chaos, no one noticed the flicker of clarity in Chen Ji's eyes—the performance was flawless.

Han Lie froze for an instant, then burst into cold laughter: 'Ha! Is this the 'talent' the Imperial Court has its eye on? Can't even control his own meridians—what a joke!' He strode forward, placing one foot on Chen Ji's hand. 'Trash is trash, deserves to die—' Yet just then, a sharp sword aura suddenly struck, forcing him to retreat repeatedly. Su Qingyao stood before Chen Ji, a longsword in hand, her chest heaving, tears glistening in her eyes: 'Chen Ji! Wake up!'

choices.description: Making the fake death more authentic, while also taking the chance to draw closer to Su Qingyao—though she doesn't know the truth, her genuine emotions deserve a response.
choices.visible_reward: Su Qingyao's affection increases, her protection grows more resolute
choices.risk_hint: If she sees through the deception, the plan may be exposed

text.content: Chen Ji's body gradually quieted from its violent tremors, yet two clear streams of tears slipped from the corners of his eyes. Those tears seemed to contain boundless regret and reluctance—many female disciples present reddened their eyes. Su Qingyao wept even more bitterly, trembling as she cradled his head in her embrace. In this moment, no one knew that the person in her arms was secretly sighing in his heart—the girl's acting was truly too good, making him feel a bit guilty.

choices.description: Already performed enough—might as well quit while ahead. Let Su Qingyao continue acting; after all, her skills surpass his.
choices.visible_cost: Miss the chance to draw closer
choices.visible_reward: The fake death becomes even more seamless
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao might grow even more suspicious of him

text.content: Chen Ji's body gradually stiffened, his breathing completely ceased. Su Qingyao held him, tears sliding silently down her face. Her fingers secretly tapped three times on his back—this was the prearranged signal between them, meaning 'Keep pretending, don't turn back.' Chen Ji silently gave her acting a perfect score in his heart. This woman, she hid her skills even deeper than he did.

dialogue.content: The entire arena erupted, buzzing with discussion. Ling Yuan narrowed his eyes, examining the 'corpse' on the ground, feeling something was off. A废物 falling to demonic possession and death should be perfectly normal, yet why did he feel everything was too smooth? He stepped forward, about to speak, when a hoarse yet authoritative voice suddenly rang out: 'Everyone, stand back! Let this old man take a look!' The Imperial Court Envoy—that old man who had remained silent all along—finally moved. He hurried to Chen Ji's side, kneeling down, his withered fingers pressing against Chen Ji's pulse.

The Imperial Court Envoy's expression drastically changed—that ancient, impassive old face actually displayed a flicker of fear. He猛地站起身, his voice carrying several degrees of trembling: 'This... this is impossible!' The Crown Prince frowned: 'What happened?' The Envoy took a deep breath, yet couldn't suppress the panic in his voice: 'His life force... has completely severed! Yet his soul fluctuation still exists—this isn't ordinary demonic possession from Qi deviation—this is—someone secretly tampered with him!' At these words, Ling Yuan's pupils constricted. Han Lie's face turned ashen—if Chen Ji was murdered, the spear would likely point at him.

'What do you mean?' Han Lie roared in anger. 'Are you implying I killed this废物?' The Imperial Court Envoy coldly gazed at him: 'This old man is merely stating facts. Young Master Han, if your conscience is clear, why be so agitated?' Han Lie trembled with rage, yet couldn't utter a word. He indeed hadn't killed Chen Ji, but now with no witness and the dead unable to speak, even jumping into the Yellow River couldn't wash away the suspicion. Ling Yuan watched coldly from the side, his mind rapidly calculating—if Chen Ji truly died on his territory, the Imperial Court would never let it rest. Someone must be held responsible...

choice.prompt: The fake death triggers chaos among all parties—how to wrap things up?

choices.description: Let the chaos continue to ferment, with all parties suspecting each other. The dead cannot speak, but the storm stirred by the dead is only beginning.
choices.visible_reward: All parties' conflicts intensify, creating conditions for subsequent schemes
choices.risk_hint: Might be discovered by a master

text.content: Chen Ji continued maintaining his stiff posture, but his consciousness remained perfectly clear. He heard the Crown Prince order a full investigation, heard Ling Yuan attempt to shirk responsibility, heard Han Lie raging and swearing vengeance. Most interestingly, he heard the Imperial Court Envoy whisper to the Crown Prince: 'This person's identity is extraordinary—the Emperor personally inquired about him... we must take the body back for autopsy.' Autopsy? Chen Ji laughed in his heart. The imperial physicians would find his body completely normal—when that time came, the real show would begin.

choices.description: Leave a slight flaw, letting certain people see hope. If the plan requires certain people to believe he's still alive, better let them see a hint first.
choices.visible_reward: Laying the groundwork for a later reversal

text.content: Just as the crowd was arguing endlessly, a sharp-eyed disciple suddenly exclaimed: 'His hand! He moved!' Everyone turned to look, only to see Chen Ji's fingers seem to slightly tremble. The Imperial Court envoy stepped forward quickly, examined carefully, then shook his head: 'It's a neural reflex, not a true sign of life.' But Su Qingyao noticed that Chen Ji's fingertips were tapping ever so covertly—a secret signal they'd agreed upon, meaning 'I'm fine, proceed as planned.' Her eyes brightened slightly, and her heart eased.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao suddenly stood up, her voice hoarse but firm: 'Regardless, we cannot leave Chen Ji's body lying here like this.' She looked at the prince. 'Your Highness, please allow me to personally escort him back to his quarters. Whether he was murdered or it was an accident, there must be an explanation.' The prince contemplated briefly, then nodded: 'Very well. Su Zhongwei values loyalty deeply, so I grant your request.' Ling Yuan wanted to intervene, but was forced back by the Imperial Court envoy's stern gaze. Eventually, a procession formed, escorting Chen Ji's 'remains' grandly toward the servants' quarters.

text.content: After the crowd dispersed, in a corner of the Martial Arena, Han Lie stood with a dark expression, muttering curses. Ling Yuan approached him quietly, lowering his voice: 'Doesn't Young Master Han find it strange? A worthless wretch going into qi deviation, why does the Imperial Court pay such attention?' Han Lie coldly snorted: 'What are you trying to say?' Ling Yuan's murky old eyes gleamed sharply: 'I'm saying, there may be hidden circumstances behind this. This Chen Ji... perhaps isn't as simple as he appears on the surface.' The two exchanged a knowing glance, with some unspoken understanding forming between them.

dialogue.content: Meanwhile, Chen Ji was carried back to the servants' quarters. Su Qingyao dismissed everyone and personally closed the doors and windows. She gazed at the motionless 'corpse' on the bed, a meaningful smile suddenly curling at the corner of her mouth: 'Everyone's gone, stop pretending.' Chen Ji remained motionless. Su Qingyao sighed, reaching out to pinch his waist. 'Hiss—' Chen Ji suddenly sat up, rubbing his waist with a grimace, 'Su Shijie, be gentle, that's my softest spot.'

Su Qingyao didn't smile, simply watching him quietly with complex eyes: 'Do you know how worried I was when you 'died'?' Chen Ji froze, then quickly shed his playful demeanor, saying seriously: 'Thank you, Su Shijie, for cooperating in the act. I'll remember this favor.' Su Qingyao turned her face away, her voice somewhat muffled: 'I wasn't acting.' As soon as she said it, she herself was stunned, seemingly not expecting to say such words. The air suddenly grew quiet, and Chen Ji stared at her slightly reddened ear tips, an indescribable emotion welling up inside him.

text.content: At that moment, hurried footsteps sounded outside the door. A Tianqing Sect disciple called out loudly: 'Su Shijie! A message from His Highness the Prince—the Imperial Court Imperial Medical Academy's Chief Physician is coming personally to examine Chen Ji's body! Please prepare, Su Shijie!' Chen Ji and Su Qingyao exchanged a glance, both seeing gravity in each other's eyes. The Fake Death Pill's effects could last at most twelve hours, yet the examination was scheduled just one hour away. The Imperial Medical Academy's Chief Physician was a renowned medical sage across the realm; deceiving his eyes would be no easy task.
